A uniform validator regression would normally fail either ~all or a specific token class; if the failing class is 'tokens signed with the pre-rotation key', then H1's own scope argument actually supports H2's mechanism. No evidence names which class, and the fraction ~1/3 is asserted from the aggregate error_rate alone. If the real split were token-class-based it would be testable; it was not tested.

The ranking lists H1 and H2 as a 0.40/0.40 tie but presents H1 as the 'active' top hypothesis. A tie is not a ranking. If the team ships the ranking as-is, the on-call gets no actionable direction and may roll back dep-5710 (which, if H2 is true, leaves the outage running).

critiques.summary: Round 3 exhausted the available evidence and, crucially, established that the discriminators are structurally unavailable rather than merely unqueried: error_rate carries no instance/replica/AZ label (F24, F40), no route/endpoint label exists on auth-service or api-gateway (F36–F38), dep-5710 has no rollout/replica fields (F30, F31, F35), no JWKS/key-publish artifact or key-store service exists in the registry (F32, F34), and auth-service logs are unsearchable due to the identity-namespace pipeline outage (F29). All three live hypotheses (H1 dep-5710 14:00:00Z, H2 cfg-2705 14:01:00Z, H6 their interaction) name an origin on auth-service, are co-timed within 60s of each other, each precede the 14:02 onset, and each predicts the SAME observables: a single clean step to a stable ~36% plateau, flat request_rate, flat CPU/mem/latency, zero restarts, and ~21% propagated to api-gateway. The automated checks flag exactly one evidence-free hop in each chain, and that hop is the mechanism that would separate them. H6 is not independent — it is a combination of H1 and H2 that produces identical observables and cannot be ranked above them on current evidence. Rounds 1–2 correctly retired the alternatives: H3 is excluded on change evidence and mechanism, H4 has no TTL/skew artifact and does not decay, H5 has no positive evidence, H7 is contradicted by flat latency/CPU/mem. So the origin is well-bounded to the auth-service 14:00–14:01 change pair, but the choice among H1/H2/H6 — which implies materially different fixes (roll back dep-5710 vs re-publish/accept both key ids) — is a coin flip that no remaining tool can break. Per the rules, uncertainty between hypotheses naming DIFFERENT origins with no obtainable tiebreaker is 'inconclusive', not a lowered-confidence 'accept'. Note the framing caveat: H1/H2/H6 all share the auth-service change window, so the safe operational move is to make the validator accept both key ids OR roll back dep-5710 and re-rotate — but that is a mitigation decision, not a proven root cause.

challenges.issue: The causal middle hop ('the rewritten validator rejects a stable class of valid tokens') is flagged by the automated check as having NO evidence. Onset at 14:02 is 2 minutes after dep-5710 (14:00:00Z), longer than the 1-minute gap to cfg-2705, so temporal order does not favour H1 — it slightly disfavours it on naive lag. No parser error text exists (F29), no per-class token evidence, and the ~1/3 share is inferred solely from the aggregate error_rate (F36, F39, F40).

The middle hop ('new key id adopted by only part of the validating surface') is both evidence-free and, per F30/F31/F32/F34/F35, UNTESTABLE on the exposed artifact surface — no rollout state, no JWKS publish timestamp, no per-replica metric. It survives only on the HIST-108 analogy (F12/F17), which the tool itself labels a lead, not evidence. F26/F27 (no decay over 1.5h) removes the self-healing refresh-lag variant and leaves only a structural split that nothing can confirm.

H6 is presented as a distinct origin but is the conjunction of H1 and H2; it adds no testable prediction beyond their union and inherits both unverified hops. The claim that jjwt 0.12 'hardened key/kid resolution or removed a fallback path' is an inference about library internals with no artifact (F29). It cannot be ranked above or below H1/H2 on current evidence and should not be counted as an independent discriminating origin.

Calibration: the ranking's 0.40/0.38/0.22 spread implies a meaningful ordering, but the three hypotheses predict identical observables and share the same onset, so the differences are prior-plausibility, not measured signal. Any single number above ~0.4 for H1 as 'the' cause is not defensible.

Confirmed rejected; residual gap is that redis-cache/user-db error_rate was never read (budget_exhausted/not_found), so H3's exclusion rests on change evidence (F11/F15) plus mechanism rather than a healthy dependency metric. The mechanism argument (fast credential-level invalid_token with flat latency/CPU) stands independently, so this is minor, not blocking.
